newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call rises as banks cover reserve positions.
newsitem.headline: Indian call rises as banks cover reserve positions.

text.p: Indian call rates ended at 8.00-9.00 percent on Thursday, after a spurt at 10.75 percent in mid-session against opening levels of 8.50-9.25 percent, dealers said.

Call rates opened at 9.0 percent, rallied briefly to 10.75 percent and closed at 8.0 percent, a dealer at a state-run bank said. "Most of the banks were short on their cash reserve requirements, which resulted in excess demand for call rates, pushing it to 10.75 percent," he said.

"We expect the cut-off yield for the forthcoming 10-year bonds at 10.65 percent, as the amount is nominal and should receive overwhelming support from insurance firms and financial institutions," said dealer R.Narayan at Bank of Nova Scotia.
The Indian Finance Ministry announced on Thursday the auction of 10 billion rupees' worth of 10-year government bonds on February 20.
"In the morning session the call rates started at higher levels," said Chandra Shetty, a dealer at Mata Securities.

"There was not much activity in the securities market, as the buyers were bidding very low rates and sellers were not ready to strike deals at those levels. During the day call started easing a bit and buyers started quoting workable rates."
The total transacted amount on National Stock Exchange was 2.0 billion rupees against the previous day's 918 million rupees, Shetty said.
The securities market saw a mixed response in tandem with call rates. The prices of securities rose in mid-session and fell towards the close, dealers said.
The 13.50 percent 1997 stock rose by 10 basis points to 103.0 rupees before settling to 102.98 rupees against its previous close, dealers said.
Treasury bills maturing in October dealt at 9.45 percent, compared to the previous yield of 7.25 percent, dealers said.
